subject: Q3 infrastructure cost review
body: Hi everyone, ahead of the planning meeting here is the full Q3 infrastructure cost review. Our AWS bill grew 18% quarter over quarter, mostly due to Lambda invocations of the parsing service and larger RDS instances that were provisioned during the September incident and never scaled back. The CDN costs stayed flat. We propose three actions: first, right-size the RDS instances back to db.r6g.large, which alone should save about $3,100 per month; second, enable provisioned concurrency only during business hours for the two latency-sensitive functions; third, move cold logs older than 30 days to S3 Glacier. Each action has an owner in the attached sheet. We also reviewed the reserved instance coverage, which dropped to 61% because two reservations expired in August; renewing them for one year at the no-upfront rate would cut compute costs by another 9%. Finance has asked for a final recommendation by the 15th so the budget for next year can be locked. Please review the numbers in the sheet, leave comments directly in the cells, and flag anything that looks wrong before Thursday. Detailed breakdown per service: compute 41%, storage 22%, database 19%, networking 11%, other 7%. Compared with last year, storage grew the fastest because of document attachments in the candidate profiles; a lifecycle policy for attachments older than two years is being discussed with the legal team because of retention requirements. Thanks for your input, the platform team.
Your package has been shipped and will arrive on Tuesday. Track it with the code in your account.
